problem: Visual point-goal navigation policies (NavDP, ViNT, DD-PPO) reach hundreds of millions of parameters and billions of frames because geometry, mapping and control are learned implicitly, which is too costly for on-device robots. Existing decomposed planners couple modules through learning and extra interface objectives, so the decomposition itself is rarely tested.
motivation: Operations with known closed-form structure (projective geometry, occupancy, coordinate transforms) need not be learned. If they are computed analytically and used as interfaces between small learned modules, the learning load and parameter count can drop sharply. The paper asks how much really needs to be learned for a single task family such as point-goal navigation.
key_idea: Factor point-goal navigation into three tiny learned modules (egress subgoal predictor, goal-conditioned navigation posterior, endpoint-pinned residual diffusion generator) connected by closed-form geometry, so only 0.58M parameters are trained.
insight: The interfaces carry the work: the ablations show removing the navigation predictor drops SR from 58.4 to 3.0 and removing the egress predictor drops it to 20.8. Training the generator on GT trajectories (34.7 SR) or jointly end-to-end (35.6) is much worse than training it on sampled posteriors, because mode-averaging is benign in density space but harmful in trajectory space. Because the subgoal is a single pixel, the encoder can be swapped for MobileNetV2 with only about a 2 SR loss, and the egress head alone can be retrained for no-goal exploration.
method: Closed-form geometry: depth is unprojected analytically into a BEV occupancy map, and a costmap is built as max(exp(-d/λ), bearing ramp). Modules exchange information through closed-form transforms, so each works in its native frame.

Egress predictor f_eg: a small head on frozen DepthAnythingV2 ViT-S features plus the goal, trained with cross-entropy over a patch grid to predict the pixel where the path to the goal exits the BEV window or is occluded. At inference it takes the argmax and ray-casts to the ground plane to get the 3D subgoal.

Navigation predictor f_np: takes the subgoal and the BEV occupancy and emits K recurrent posterior maps with per-cell heading. Its targets anneal from a straight-line prior to the GT path, with a collision penalty on the final map, and at test time frontier cost is raised after a collision.

Generator f_gen: a DDPM (10 steps, x0-prediction plus a collision cost) that denoises B-spline residuals around the straight line to the egress endpoint. It is conditioned on the posterior, subgoal and velocity, and trained on paths sampled from the f_np posterior instead of GT.
Critic: post-hoc deterministic selection among N sampled trajectories, minimizing mean exponential obstacle-distance cost along the path.
Training: about 44k single-frame states from 55 Matterport3D scenes, under one GPU-hour on an RTX 4090; only 0.58M of 22.7M parameters are trained.

setting.backbone: Frozen DepthAnythingV2 ViT-S encoder + small trained egress / navigation predictor / DDPM generator (0.58M trainable); variant with MobileNetV2 encoder
setting.training_data: about 44k random single-frame states from 55 Matterport3D scenes with GT trajectories (0-6 m horizon)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB + depth, plus localization-derived velocity and goal (cuVSLAM in real world)
setting.action_space: predicted B-spline trajectories (waypoints) in BEV, selected by a critic
setting.simulator: Isaac Sim (InternRobotics / NavDP benchmark: InternScenes + ClutteredEnv); Matterport3D for training
setting.privileged: none at test time in the real world; in simulation the point-goal and localization are given (oracle localization in sim; cuVSLAM in real)

numbers.extra: trained on 44k MP3D frames; Home suite over 2k episodes

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjectNav benchmarks; results are on the InternRobotics (NavDP) point-goal benchmark. MBNetv2 rows for the other suites: Commercial 68.4/62.9, Clut.-Easy 87.6/79.7, Clut.-Hard 79.7/70.7 (SR/SPL). The split label 'test' is a placeholder since the benchmark has no official split names.
results: On 6060 point-goal episodes the system reaches 70.1 average SR with only 0.58M trainable parameters, beating ViPlanner (59.3) and iPlanner (59.9) and trailing NavDP (73.8, 135.7M parameters) by about 3.7 SR. It has the lowest collision rate (0.111 per 10 m vs 0.173-0.237) and runs zero-shot on a Jetson Orin Nano at about 20 Hz.
limitations: Restricted to single-floor navigation because of depth-derived BEV maps; multi-floor needs voxel or 3D representations.
Fragile under heavy depth Gaussian noise (σ=0.05z², 19% relative SR) because the analytic BEV fails; it is fixed with a 3x3 median filter.
Image-goal navigation is untested; ablations use only 101 episodes; still trails NavDP in SR, and the real-world evaluation is only qualitative.
